newsitem.title: INDIA: Rice paddy fungus could combat mosquito.
newsitem.headline: Rice paddy fungus could combat mosquito.

text.p: Indian scientists have isolated a fungus found in rice paddy fields that could be used in the fight against malaria and other mosquito-borne diseases, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said on Sunday.
Dr Ashwini Kumar of the Malaria Research Centre in the southern state of Goa told the news agency that the fungus, named MRC-367, can kill mosquito larvae in three hours.
"Of the 200 microbes we screened in last six months, this is the most promising biocontrol agent against mosquitoes," Dr D. Thavaselvam of the centre told PTI.
The news agency said the quick-growing fungus could be used to combat diseases such as malaria and dengue, which kill thousands of people every year in India.

Dr Kumar said experiments had so far been carried out only in the laboratory. "We have to make sure it is safe for non-target organisms like fish before we can carry out field trials," he was quoted as saying.
